h1: Best cleaners in Leeds: 3 local house cleaning companies
checks: Ask whether cleaners are employed by the firm or self employed, and whether they are DBS checked.
Ask whether the firm has public liability insurance in case something is damaged.
Agree what is included in a clean, such as ironing, oven or windows, and the hourly rate, in writing.

p: You can hire a cleaner through a cleaning company, an agency that introduces self employed cleaners, or directly. A cleaning company that employs its staff usually handles holiday cover, insurance and vetting for you. With an agency or a private cleaner, check who is responsible if something goes wrong.
Whoever you choose, ask for references or read reviews that mention regular cleans over several months, not just one visit.

ul: Regular cleaning: weekly or fortnightly, usually charged by the hour.
Deep cleaning: a one off top to bottom clean, including inside cupboards, skirting boards and appliances.
End of tenancy cleaning: a thorough clean when you move out of a rented home, often to an agent's checklist.
After builders cleaning: dust and debris after a renovation.

guide.h2: What to agree before the first clean
ul: The hourly rate and minimum hours per visit
Who supplies cleaning products and equipment
How keys are kept and returned
What happens if a clean is missed or something is damaged
How much notice either side must give to stop

p: Most house cleaners vacuum but do not deep clean carpets or sofas. For that, see our list of carpet cleaning firms in Leeds and the typical prices in our carpet cleaning cost guide.

ul: Domestic cleaning: regular weekly or fortnightly home cleaning
Deep cleaning services: a one off clean of kitchens, bathrooms and appliances
End of tenancy cleaning: often to a letting agent's checklist, sometimes with oven and carpet cleaning
Office cleaning and commercial cleaning: early morning or evening cleans
Oven cleaning, carpet and upholstery cleaning: often done by specialists

guide.h2: How to choose a cleaning company in Leeds
p: Start with what you need: a regular domestic cleaner, a one off deep clean or an end of tenancy clean in a student area such as Headingley or Hyde Park. Ask two or three cleaning companies for a price and what is included. Read customer reviews that mention the same cleaner over months, and ask whether the firm brings its own cleaning products. A good cleaning business will give you a clear booking process and one point of contact.

faqs.q: Should a cleaner be DBS checked?
faqs.a: It is not a legal requirement for domestic cleaners, but many cleaning companies DBS check their staff. If someone will have keys to your home, it is reasonable to ask.

faqs.q: Do I need to provide cleaning products?
faqs.a: It depends on the firm. Some bring everything, others use your products and equipment. Agree this before the first clean.

faqs.q: What is included in a deep clean?
faqs.a: Usually everything in a regular clean plus areas that are often missed, such as inside cupboards and appliances, behind furniture, skirting boards, doors and light switches. Ask for a checklist.

faqs.q: Can I get the same cleaner each week?
faqs.a: Many companies try to send the same cleaner or team for regular cleans. Ask how they cover holidays and sickness.

faqs.q: How often should I book a cleaner?
faqs.a: Weekly or fortnightly suits most busy households. A deep clean once or twice a year keeps on top of areas a regular clean misses.
